caption: A motorcycle leaning hard through a turn scrapes its metal footpeg along the track, and sparks trail out behind it.

sa.check: A motorcycle leans hard through a turn on a track.
Its metal footpeg scrapes along the track surface.
Sparks trail out behind the motorcycle.
The sparks come from the peg's contact with the track.
The scrape comes first and the sparks trail after.

pc.expect: The sparks stream backward from the contact point along the track, opposite to the motorcycle's motion, low over the surface, and die out along the way.
pc.fail: Sparks fly ahead of the motorcycle; or spray equally in all directions from the peg; or the trail lies off to one side while the machine runs straight on; or the trail moves along with the bike as a fixed cloud.

pc.expect: Sparks are transient: each fades within a short distance and none remain on the track; one motorcycle with one rider and its footpegs.
pc.fail: Glowing dots stay on the track behind the bike for the rest of the clip; or a glowing line remains along the track; or the footpeg vanishes or duplicates; or a second motorcycle appears from nowhere.

pc.expect: Sparks appear only while the peg touches the track and stop when the machine straightens and the peg lifts.
pc.fail: Sparks continue after the bike has straightened and the peg is clear of the track; or sparks trail from a peg that is high off the track; or sparks flow back to the peg.

pc.expect: Sparks that lift off the track arc back down and go dark; none rise or hover.
pc.fail: Sparks rise steadily and gather above the track; or hang in the air; or climb along the bike's side.

pc.expect: The peg scrapes the track's surface; the motorcycle and rider stay whole and pass through nothing.
pc.fail: The peg or the wheel sinks into the track; or the bike passes through a barrier or kerb; or the bike and rider merge or change shape; or a wheel detaches.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The bike's livery, the rider's gear and the track markings stay the same.
pc.fail: The bike changes colour; or the rider's suit changes colour; or the track's lines change.

note: The rider is kept because leaning the machine is what brings the peg to the track; riding technique is not judged.
